domains.proposed_domain: Mathematical physics and quantum tensor-network representations

evidence.quote: Preparing the initial vector is permitted because we seek a representation, rather than an algorithm for finding it.

exclusions.reason: The protocol may begin with the ground vector supplied privately, and the representation theorem provides no efficient tensor-discovery guarantee.

evidence.quote: The theorem makes no claim that its tensors can be found or contracted efficiently; their entries may depend arbitrarily on $H$ and $\Omega$.

exclusions.query: Efficient contraction of the approximating PEPS
exclusions.reason: The theorem does not establish an efficient contraction method for its particular approximants.

evidence.quote:
Suppose that $H$ has a unique normalized ground vector $\Omega$, up to phase, with ground energy $E_0$, and $$\label{eq:global-gap}

exclusions.query: Uniform approximation guarantee for gapless or degenerate ground states
exclusions.reason: A fixed positive full-system gap and a unique normalized ground vector are required; the conclusion is not established outside those assumptions.

evidence.quote: For an integer $L\ge2$, let $\Lambda_L=\{1,\ldots,L\}^2$, with the nearest-neighbor square-lattice edge set $E(\Lambda_L)$ and open boundary conditions.

exclusions.query: Original-grid PEPS bound on a torus or arbitrary interaction graph
exclusions.reason: The proved representation concerns bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions on an open square.

evidence.quote: The theorem here concerns the full vector and imposes no such structural requirements on the approximant.

exclusions.query: Injective approximant with a gapped parent Hamiltonian
exclusions.reason: The representation conclusion imposes no such structural requirements.

evidence.quote: The representation theorem uses the full companion interface recorded in Appendix 9, rather than the cutwise entropy inequality alone.

exclusions.query: Entropy area law alone implies compatible efficient global tensor approximation
exclusions.reason: The proof requires the stronger companion interfaces and compatible operations in addition to cutwise entropy control.

outputs.exact_statement: Under [eq:model]–[eq:global-gap], there is $C_A=C_A(q,J,\Delta)$ such that every $A\subseteq\Lambda$ satisfies $$S_\Omega(A)\le C_A|\partial_\Lambda A|, \qquad \partial_\Lambda A=\{\{x,y\}\in E(\Lambda):x\in A, \ y\notin A\}.$$ The same constant works for every $L$ and every Hamiltonian in the class.

For normalized finite-dimensional states, $$\label{eq:fidelity-information}
 F(\rho,\sigma)\ge e^{-D(\rho\Vert\sigma)/2},
 \qquad
 D(\rho_{AC}\Vert\rho_A\otimes\rho_C)=I(A:C),$$ Moreover, after enlarging the purifying space if necessary, an isometry on that space realizes overlap $F(\rho,\sigma)$ between purifications. In particular a mutual-information bound $\delta$ gives purifications of the joint state and product state at vector distance at most $\sqrt\delta$, after phase choice, since $2(1-e^{-\delta/2})\le\delta$.

Fix an integer $N_0\ge1$ and a constant $A_0\ge1$. There are $\beta<1$, $C<\infty$, and $u_0<\infty$ such that the following holds. Let $u\ge u_0$ and let $T$ be the full ambient lattice sample of a union of at most $N_0$ axis-parallel rectangles, with $\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_\infty T\le A_0u$. For every physical set $E\subseteq\Lambda$ satisfying $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(E,T)>u^\beta,$$ one has $$I_\Omega(\Lambda\cap T:E)\le C.$$ The same statement holds for any subset of $\Lambda\cap T$ in its first argument, for rectangles with consistently assigned open or closed sides, and after a common translation of the lattice coordinates.

Fix $c>0$. Tile the plane by an axis-parallel grid of squares of side $s\ge1$. Let $G$ be the physical sample of one cell, let $B$ be the physical sample of any union of other cells, and let $C\subseteq\Lambda\setminus(B\cup G)$ satisfy $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(C,\overline{G}_{\rm amb})\ge cs,$$ where $\overline{G}_{\rm amb}$ denotes the full closed ambient cell. There are fixed constants $C_1,K<\infty$ such that $$I_\Omega(G:C\mid B)\le C_1(1+\log s)^K.
 \label{eq:info-cell-cmi}$$ The constants are independent of which exterior cells comprise $B$ and of the shape of $C$ away from the cell.

For every fixed $p>0$ there is $C_p<\infty$ with the following property for all sufficiently large $L$. Let $R,C\subseteq\Lambda$ be disjoint, let $R_0\subseteq R$ and $C_0\subseteq C$, and suppose $$I_\Omega(R:C)\le b,\qquad b\ge0.$$ If $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(R_0,\Lambda\setminus R)>w,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(C_0,\Lambda\setminus C)>w,
 \qquad w=C_p(1+b+\log L),
 \label{eq:info-reset-width}$$ then $$I_\Omega(R_0:C_0)\le L^{-p}.$$ Only the original full-system gap is assumed.

Fix $a>0$, $A_0\ge1$, an integer $m_0\ge0$, and $p>0$. There is $D<\infty$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $L$. Let $\mathcal V$ be a set of at most $m_0$ marked points in the plane, let $X,E\subseteq\Lambda$ be disjoint, and let $$D\log L\le n\le A_0L,
 \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_\infty X\le A_0n.$$ Put $s_{\min}=D\log L$ and $d_{\mathcal V}(x)=\min_{v\in\mathcal V}|x-v|_\infty$, with $d_{\varnothing}=+\infty$. Suppose that for every $x\in X$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(x,E)
   \ge a\max\{s_{\min},\min(n,d_{\mathcal V}(x))\}.
 \label{eq:info-angular-separation}$$ Then $$I_\Omega(X:E)\le L^{-p}.$$ The constant $D$ and the scale threshold are uniform in the marked points, physical sets, and Hamiltonian.

Let $G$ be a contraction with an expansion $G=\sum_{\xi}c_{\xi}M_{\xi}$ into $K$ allowed monomials on a fixed set of parties. Suppose each monomial has at most $r$ pair effects. For every integer $m\ge1$ there is a gate $\widetilde G_m$, with additional garbage registers, and a fixed normalized garbage vector $\Gamma_m$, such that $$\lVert \widetilde G_m-G\otimes|\Gamma_m\rangle\rVert
 \le \frac{r}{\sqrt m}\sum_{\xi}|c_{\xi}|.
 \label{eq:compression-effect-error}$$ The gate $\widetilde G_m$ has an expansion using only local contractions and normalized pair sources. It has at most $K m^r$ monomials, and their absolute coefficient sum is at most $\sum_{\xi}|c_{\xi}|$. Its additional registers are owned by the original participating parties. All sources on the same pair of parties may be combined into one normalized pair source.

Consider a family of distributed constructions indexed by $L\ge2$ with the following uniform properties.*

1.  *The number of parties and gates is uniformly polynomial. The initial vector is a tensor product of normalized private vectors, one at each party, and every gate is a contraction.*

2.  *There is a constant $b$ such that each nonprivate gate involves at most $b$ parties, and each party participates in at most $b$ nonprivate gates over the entire construction.*

3.  *Each nonprivate gate is a sum of uniformly polynomially many allowed monomials with uniformly polynomially bounded scalar coefficients. There is a constant $r$ bounding the number of pair sources, pair effects, and polynomial-dimensional messages in each monomial. All constituent local maps are contractions.*

4.  *At the end, the intended physical output space of each party has uniformly polynomial dimension. All other registers are traced out party by party.*

*Write $\rho$ for the resulting physical output density operator; it is positive and may have trace less than one. For every fixed $p>0$, there is an operator tensor network $\sigma$ satisfying $$\lVert \sigma-\rho\rVert_1\le L^{-p}.$$ It has one node per party, a bounded number of incident virtual links at each node, and uniformly polynomial link dimensions. Every link joins two parties which participate in a common nonprivate gate of the original construction. The physical legs at a node are the ket and bra legs of that party’s intended output. The constants in these bounds depend only on $p$ and the fixed uniform data in the assumptions, including $b,r$ and the polynomial bounds, and not on private dimensions or source Schmidt ranks.*

*The same conclusion holds if the gate expansions in the third assumption are available to every fixed inverse-polynomial operator-norm accuracy, with uniform polynomial bounds at each fixed accuracy.

Consider old and new one-sheet frames. Only a bounded number of their holes are affected; all other holes, encodings, and tag owners agree. Suppose there are $m=O(1)$ additional square patches $(c_i,u_i)$, with $00$, $M$ admits a contractive approximation $M_a$ with $\lVert M_a-M\rVert\le L^{-a}$ and a polynomial sum expansion of the kind required by Theorem 10, using only the specified parties. In particular the rewrite is a bounded change with reference-vector error $O(L^{-20})$.

For all sufficiently large $L$, there is a protocol with the following properties. All constants in this statement are uniform in the Hamiltonian and $L$.* 1. *There are $O(L^2)$ parties, one for each square in a padded dyadic hierarchy and at most a fixed number of additional parties for each repainting of a square. Initialization is a pure product across parties. One party initially holds the main copy of $\Omega$; all auxiliary copies are initialized privately at their designated parties.* 2. *The schedule has at most $C L^3$ changes. Each change is implemented by a fixed number of contraction gates involving at most a fixed number of parties and having the bipartite-resource expansions established in Lemmas 14, 16, and 17. The expansions can be made accurate to any fixed inverse power of $L$ in operator norm where an approximation is needed. Each party participates in at most a fixed number of gates involving other parties over its entire lifetime.* 3. *Every linked gate involves parties at the same or adjacent dyadic scales. Parties at a gate have addresses at distance $O(n)$ from one another, where $n$ is either endpoint scale; additional parties have the scale and address of the square to whose repainting they belong.* 4. *There is a designated reference vector at every stage, formed from the main encoded frame and the auxiliary encoded frames. All its factors have norm at most one. Each change takes its preceding reference vector within $C L^{-20}$ in vector norm of its following reference vector. At the end, the reference is $$\Omega\otimes\Xi, \qquad 1-C L^{3-60}\le \lVert \Xi\rVert\le1,$$ where $\Xi$ contains only registers to be discarded. Every original physical site is a raw register at its own unit-square party. No other party has a physical output, so every party’s physical output dimension is at most $q$.

There is a fixed $a_0>0$ such that every unmodified elementary birth or death above has changed region $R$ of diameter $O(n)$ and surrounding guide $f$ satisfying $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\bigl(y,\overline{\{f\ne P_\circ\}}\bigr)
 \ge a_0\min\{n,d_{\mathcal V}(y)\},
 \qquad y\in\overline R.
 \label{eq:geometry-birth-clearance}$$ For an unmodified lens exchange, every point in the closure of the positions that are not common $C$ on its two before guides satisfies $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(y,\partial Y)
 \ge a_0\min\{n,d_{\mathcal V}(y)\}.
 \label{eq:geometry-exchange-clearance}$$ Here and throughout this section distances are ambient sup distances.

Let $\Omega$ be a unit vector on a tensor product of finite-dimensional spaces. If an operator $\sigma$ satisfies $\lVert \sigma-|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|\rVert_1\le\eta<1$, then some product-basis column $v=\sigma|z\rangle$ is nonzero and satisfies $$\min_\theta\left\|\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}-e^{i\theta}\Omega\right\|
 \le2\eta.$$ Fixing this column in an operator tensor network leaves all its virtual dimensions unchanged.

The links of the party network can be routed on the padded grid with constant edge congestion. After reflection into the genuine $L\times L$ grid, congestion is still constant and physical output coordinates are unchanged.
